description: Hand-written earlier session in this repository (synthetic: the requests, thoughts, and answers were written for receipts-bench; every tool output was captured by running the step on the starting repository).

episodes.request: Our logs show an error with the message `2 listeners of "layout:saved" failed: widget crashed; timeout`. Which class is that, and what else does it carry besides the message? No changes, please.

steps.thought: The message format is built in the error class; read it.
Check how the message and the fields are covered by tests.

finish.thought: The class and its fields are all in errors.ts.
finish.report: That is EmitError, defined in src/errors.ts. Besides the message it carries event (the name of the event whose listeners failed, for example layout:saved) and errors (everything the failing listeners threw, in the order the listeners were called, whatever the thrown values are), and its name is EmitError. The message is built from the number of failures (`1 listener` or `N listeners`), the event name in JSON quotes, and the message of each error, or String(value) for anything that is not an Error, joined with `; `, which gives `2 listeners of "layout:saved" failed: widget crashed; timeout`. test/errors.test.ts checks the message format and that errors keeps the order.

episodes.request: How does waitFor clean up when the event never comes? The refresh button uses it, and I want to be sure it does not leak listeners.

finish.thought: Both ways out of waitFor remove the listener.
finish.report: It does not leak. waitFor in src/wait.ts registers one listener with on and starts a timer. When the event comes first, the listener calls the function on returned (stop), clears the timer, and resolves with the payload. When the timer fires first, it calls stop and rejects with a WaitTimeoutError whose message is `no "<event>" event within <timeoutMs> ms`; the limit is 5000 ms unless you pass one. Either way the listener is removed.

episodes.request: Which events can a plugin listen to on the dashboard bus, and what does forward do with them? I want to mirror a plugin's bus onto the dashboard.

steps.thought: The event list is in events.ts.
The helper tests show how forward is used.

finish.thought: events.ts, forward.ts and the helper test answer both parts.
finish.report: Plugins can listen to the four dashboard events listed in DASHBOARD_EVENTS in src/events.ts: widget:added (widgetId, kind), widget:removed (widgetId), layout:saved (layoutId, widgets), and data:refreshed (source, rows). createDashboardBus makes a bus for them. forward(from, to, events) in src/forward.ts listens on the plugin's bus for each listed event (a name listed twice is forwarded once) and re-emits it on the dashboard bus with the same payload; events that are not listed are not forwarded. It returns a function that stops all of the forwarding. forward and the other helpers are exported from src/index.ts, and test/helpers.test.ts shows both buses in use.

episodes.request: Last question: how many tests cover the helpers and the listener errors?

steps.thought: The test files use top-level test() calls only, so counting them is enough.

finish.report: 10 tests: 6 in test/helpers.test.ts and 4 in test/errors.test.ts. Every test in these files is a top-level test() call, so the counts are exact.
